page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48-lssd is an arm64-based server instance powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of the Neoverse-V2 CPU architecture. It features 192 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance is equipped with 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while lacking any integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-level support for AES cryptography.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 87014.41 and a PassMark CPU physics score of 13183.99. Memory performance is highly competitive, achieving a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3183.47 and a read-only small-block memory bandwidth of 5935.14 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are particularly notable, with PassMark database operations reaching 48182.95 and static web serving throughput measured at 97.21 GB/sec, both ranking in the top tier. Redis SET operations perform strongly at 98.12 million operations per second.

Given its high-density local NVMe SSD storage and top-tier database performance, this server is highly optimized for database management systems, high-throughput web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks. The arm64 architecture offers a cost-efficient alternative to x86-based instances by delivering high resource density and strong multi-core throughput per unit of power. However, workloads requiring specialized x86 instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX will face compatibility limitations, as these features are absent.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48-lssd is an arm64 server featuring 48 dedicated Neoverse-V2 physical cores, 192 GB of RAM, and 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance delivers strong multi-core performance, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 87014.41 and a top-tier PassMark database operations score of 48182.95. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 5935.14 GB/sec for small-block reads and achieving a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3183.47. The server is optimized for high-throughput database workloads, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing. It offers a resource-dense, qualitatively cost-efficient profile for arm64-native applications, though it lacks x86-specific vector extensions and dedicated GPU acceleration.
